First public preview of **3D Piano Performances**: a live 3D/WebXR piano concert stage with a webcam- and MIDI-driven avatar, recording archive, and the optional **Performer Studio** desktop mixer.

## Downloads

| File | For |
| --- | --- |
| `3D-Piano-Performances-server-*.zip` | The stage server (any OS with Python 3.9+). Unzip, then run `setup/setup-server.sh` (macOS/Linux) or `setup\setup-server.cmd` (Windows). See `docs/server-setup.md`. |
| `Performer-Studio-*-win-x64.zip` | Performer Studio for Windows 10/11 x64. Unzip and run `Performer Studio.exe`. |
| `Performer-Studio-*-macos-arm64.zip` | Performer Studio for Apple Silicon Macs (macOS 12+). |
| `Performer-Studio-*-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Performer Studio for 64-bit Linux. Extract and run `./performer-studio`. |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | Checksums for every download. |

Visitors and browser-only performers need nothing from this page: they just open the stage in Chrome or Edge.

## Before you run the desktop app

These preview builds are **not code-signed**:

- **Windows:** SmartScreen may say *Windows protected your PC*. Click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** after unzipping, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "Performer Studio.app"` once, or right-click the app → **Open**.
- **Linux:** if it stops with a *SUID sandbox helper* message, see `README-LINUX.txt` inside the folder.

## Status

The macOS build is tested with Pianoteq 9 and UADx plug-ins. The Windows (ASIO/WASAPI) and Linux (ALSA/JACK) builds are compiled automatically and have not yet been tested on real hardware. Please report what works and what doesn't in the issues.
